passages.text: Salvia chinensis (the Chinese sage) is an annual plant that is native to several provinces in China, growing in forests, and in tufts of grass on hillsides or plains at {{convert|100|to|500|m|ft|abbr=on}} elevation. S. chinensis grows on stems that are erect or prostrate to a height of {{convert|20|to|60|cm|in|abbr=on}}. Inflorescences are 6-flowered verticillasters in terminal racemes or panicles, with a {{convert|1|cm|in|abbr=on}} blue-purple or purple corolla.
